wu: Students stand in a circle. Teacher tosses a ball to a student and says 'I like playing football.' The student catches it and says their own sentence, e.g., 'I love reading books,' then tosses the ball to another student.
wuAlt: Students play 'Two Truths and a Lie' about hobbies: 'I like swimming, I love painting, I hate cooking.' Others guess the lie.
Teacher shows flashcards of hobbies; students race to say 'I like/love/hate + -ing' for each.
pres: Teacher writes 'I like swimming' on the board. Elicits the pattern 'like + -ing'. Teaches 'love/hate + -ing' with gestures. Models: 'I love hiking, I hate cleaning.' Checks understanding by asking 'Do you like or hate studying English?'
presAlt: Teacher tells a short story: 'Last weekend, I loved eating pizza, but I hated doing homework.' Students identify the verb patterns.
Students match hobby pictures to sentences: 'I love playing video games' vs 'I hate tidying my room'.
prac: Students work in pairs. They receive a 'Hobbies Bingo' card with phrases like 'likes dancing' or 'hates studying'. Teacher calls out sentences; students mark the card and say 'Yes, I do!' or 'No, I don't!' when they get a line.
pracAlt: Students play 'Find Someone Who': walk around asking 'Do you like + -ing?' and writing names. Teacher monitors for correct verb forms.
Teacher gives a 'Verb Pattern Maze' worksheet; students trace the path from 'like' to correct -ing forms.
ls: Students listen to a short audio of a boy talking about his weekend: 'I always play football on Saturdays. Sometimes I visit my friends. I never watch TV.' They tick the activities he does and circle the adverbs.
re: Students play 'Simon Says' with verb patterns: 'Simon says: pretend you like swimming!' Students mime the action. 'Simon says: pretend you hate cleaning!' Incorrect movers sit down.
prod: In groups, students create a 'Green March Timeline Poster' with 3-4 events in the past simple (e.g., 'People walked to the capital,' 'They carried Moroccan flags'). They present their timeline to the class, using 'Our group liked working together.'
rw: Students read a short text about a teen's hobbies: 'Sara loves painting. She sometimes draws in the park. She never plays video games.' They underline all 'like/love/hate + -ing' and circle the adverbs.
st: Teacher sings a simple song about hobbies: 'I like, like, like swimming! Love, love, love reading! Hate, hate, hate cleaning!' End with: 'Today we talked about hobbies using like/love/hate + -ing. Thank you, class!'
g: Students act out a hobby (e.g., 'playing football') while others guess using 'Do you like + -ing?'
Teams race to write 'like/love/hate + -ing' on the board for teacher-called hobbies.
Students jump on squares marked 'always/sometimes/never' and say a sentence with that adverb.
Students ask 5 classmates 'Do you like + -ing?' and tally results.
Match 'walked' to 'They walked to the capital' for Green March events.
diff: Fast finishers write 5 more sentences about their hobbies using 'always/sometimes/never'.
Support weaker learners use sentence frames: 'I like/love/hate _______ing. I always/sometimes/never _______.'
hw: Read the short hobbies text and write 5 new words in your notebook.
Write 5 past-simple sentences about the Green March (e.g., 'People walked to the city.', 'They carried flags.')
Ask your family about their hobbies and write 3 sentences using 'like/love/hate + -ing'.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references like the Green March to make past simple practice meaningful; teens connect better when local history is part of the lesson.
